findings.title: Second `downsize` definition silently replaces the (from, to, max_width, max_height) version
findings.body: The PR adds `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` but leaves the existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 in place. Ruby does not overload by arity, so the later definition replaces the earlier one and the 4-argument form becomes dead. Any caller that passes width and height separately now fails: `downsize(src, dst, 500, 500, force_aspect_ratio: true)` raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments), and `downsize(src, dst, 500, 500)` passes 500 as `opts`, so `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` fails with a TypeError. Either remove the old method and migrate its callers, or keep a single definition that accepts both forms.

findings.title: Downsize loop ignores failures and never verifies the final size before uploading
findings.body: The loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize at most five times and then continues to Upload.create_for with whatever is in tempfile. Two problems. First, nothing re-checks tempfile.size against max_image_size_kb after the loop, so an image that is still over the limit is stored. Each pass scales both dimensions by 0.8 (pixel count by 0.64), so five passes leave about 11% of the original pixels, which is not enough for a large original. Second, downsize returns false when convert exits non-zero (convert_with does not log that case), and the return value is discarded. A failing conversion is retried five times on an unchanged file and the failure is invisible. On this path nothing enforces max_image_size_kb for uploaded images any more.

findings.title: API URL downloads are now capped at a hardcoded 10 MB instead of max_image_size_kb
findings.body: The download cap changes from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to a hardcoded 10.megabytes. Consequences: (a) a site that sets max_image_size_kb above 10 MB can no longer fetch images between 10 MB and its own limit through the API URL path, which contradicts the setting; (b) the new downsizing cannot help images above 10 MB fetched by URL, which is the case the feature is for; (c) when FileHelper.download fails or exceeds the cap, the `rescue nil` leaves tempfile nil, and line 72 then calls `tempfile.size` on nil and raises NoMethodError, giving a 500 rather than a validation error. The 10 MB value is also duplicated in utilities.js with no shared source.

findings.title: Client-side size limit replaced with hardcoded 10 MB for images and attachments, ignoring site settings
findings.body: The `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` lookup is replaced by a hardcoded 10 MB for every upload type. Consequences: images larger than max_image_size_kb now pass client validation up to 10 MB, and an admin who sets max_image_size_kb above 10 MB can never upload between 10 MB and that limit from the UI, so the setting above 10 MB has no effect. Attachments are now checked against 10 MB instead of max_attachment_size_kb, so attachments the admin has forbidden pass client validation. The 413 branch (line 246) also now always reports '10 MB' regardless of configuration. If the goal is to let large images through for server-side shrinking, only the image limit should change, and attachments should keep using their setting.

findings.title: Up to five ImageMagick and ImageOptim passes per oversized upload, run inline on the synchronous API path
findings.body: Each loop iteration runs a full convert pass, and convert_with also runs ImageOptim.new.optimize_image! on the output, so an oversized upload can cost five decode/encode cycles plus five optimizer runs. On the synchronous API path (`synchronous` param) this runs inline in the request and blocks the web worker for the duration. This code does not bound the input size: the client-side check is browser-only, the URL path cap is 10 MB, and the multipart path has no size check in this diff. A very large image makes every pass expensive.

findings.title: Downsizing writes in place to the uploaded file, so a failed pass can corrupt the only copy
findings.body: OptimizedImage.downsize is called with the same path as input and output, so ImageMagick overwrites the uploaded file in place. If a pass fails partway (disk full, process killed, ImageMagick error during write), the file is left truncated or corrupt. Because the return value is ignored (see the loop above), the damaged file is then passed to Upload.create_for. Writing to a separate temp file and replacing the original only on success would avoid this.

findings.title: Oversized animated GIFs are flattened to their first frame when allow_animated_thumbnails is off
findings.body: The loop reuses the thumbnail setting `allow_animated_thumbnails` for the user's original upload. When that setting is off, OptimizedImage.optimize uses downsize_instructions, which reads `#{from}[0]`, so an oversized animated GIF is replaced by a static first frame. The animation is lost permanently in the stored upload, and the user is not told. This may be intended, but it is not documented or surfaced anywhere in the PR.

findings.title: No specs for the changed downsize/optimize signatures or the new upload downsizing path
findings.body: The PR changes the signatures of optimize, resize and downsize, removes the public OptimizedImage.dimensions helper, and adds a loop in UploadsController#create_upload. No spec changes accompany any of this. A single spec calling downsize with width and height would have caught the duplicate-definition bug, and nothing covers the '80%' percentage path, the loop's termination, or the behaviour when convert fails.
